Question: This summer I will be hired as a Graduate Reserach Assistant. What course do I need to register for?
Answer: Students who are supported by the University as research assistants during the summer months are required to be registered in at least three credits during the 7 1/2 week summer session under the following guidelines: the work must be related to the student's degree program, and the funding amount must meet the minimum requirement per month in June and July. Students may register in 868-800 (research), 869 (thesis), 964 (pre-candidacy study), 969 (dissertation), 864 (internship), sustaining, or a regular graduate course needed for the degree and offered in the 7 1/2 week summer session. Except for 864, 869, or regular courses, all courses are graded pass/fail.

Question: I'm a doctoral student and my status has not changed to Sustaining. When will my status change to Sustaining?
Answer: Once a graduate student who is completing a thesis, dissertation, or education leadership portfolio has completed registration in all required course credits needed for the degree (including the registration of six credits of Master's thesis [869] or nine to twelve credits of dissertation [969]) and all other degree requirements except the submission of the thesis, dissertation, or education leadership portfolio) the student must maintain matriculation in the degree program during the fall and spring semesters by registering for either Master's Sustaining: Thesis (UNIV 899) or Doctoral Sustaining (UNIV 999). All students, including sustaining students, must be registered in the semester in which the degree is officially awarded. Sustaining registration is required for summer and winter session only if the degree is awarded at the conclusion of the summer or winter session. Students in sustaining status are considered full-time.

Answer: If you've submitted the CISC Registration Help Form and haven't seen the course added to your schedule after four days, it's advisable to follow up with the Department of Computer and Information Sciences. You can contact the department directly or reach out to your academic advisor for assistance in expediting the registration process.

Answer: To reserve a room at the STAR Campus for your preliminary exam, you fill out the request for student space form.

Question: Currently in my 1st semester MS in computer science. Reaching out to clarify the minimum grade requirements for both the breadth components and elective courses for students enrolled in Fall 2024. I want to ensure that I am meeting all necessary academic standards and expectations for these components.
Answer: For the MS in Computer Science program at the University of Delaware, students are required to complete 12 credits of elective courses, which must be taken using the standard grading option (i.e., letter grades). A minimum grade of C- is required in all CISC courses to meet degree requirements.

Question: I'm writing to see if I can schedule some time with you for some academic advising regarding the PhD program and also course selection as currently I'm facing some problems and I'm trying to solve it.
Answer: To schedule an academic advising appointment for the PhD program, please email your assigned advisor directly or schedule an appointment online through Stellic. You can find your advisor's name listed on your UDSIS account under the Degrees & Advisement tile.

Question: I am sorry for needing to re-clarify the problem I am currently encountering. I have received an admission offer for the PhD graduate program, and I need to activate my UD email account. However, when I follow the enrollment instructions, it seems to require a deposit to continue the process. I asked for help from my friends at UD, and they did not have to pay a deposit. In the error message, the deposit does not appear to be the application fee, which I already paid when I submitted my application. Am I misunderstanding something? What should I do next?
Answer: To activate your UD email account, you must first submit your admission deposit. After submitting the deposit, you can set up your UDelNet ID and password by logging into My Blue Hen Home and selecting the 'Set-up your UD email account' option. If you believe there is an error or if you have questions about the deposit requirement, please contact the Graduate College or the Center for Global Programs & Services (CGPS) for assistance.
